newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- SEARS PAYS OFF CHIEF AND ACTS TO STEM LOSSES

British-based retail conglomerate Sears has moved to stem losses in its 465 million stg a year footwear business, and has parted company with the group's chief executive, Liam Strong. Sears also revealed plans to de-merge its London department store, Selfridges, next year and announced an agreement to sell the Freemans mail order house to rival Littlewoods for 367.5 million stg.
-- SFO PROBES PAYMENT BY REGAN COMPANY IN 1995

An investigation has been launched by the Serious Fraud Office into a 2.4 million stg commission payment made as part of a deal two years ago between the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) and a company headed by Andrew Regan, the businessman forced to abandon a bid for the CWS last week. The probe centres on a payment made by food manufacturer Hobson when CWS agreed to extend a contract to buy supplies from it.
-- BOEING BACKS 'INTERNET IN SKY'

Aerospace group Boeing has joined a $9 billion venture to launch more than 300 communications satellites in order to cover the globe with Internet, business and interactive media services. Boeing is paying $100 million for a 10 per cent stake in Teledesic, a company set up by telecoms entrepreneur Craig McCaw. The third major partner in the 'Internet in the sky' venture is Bill Gates, founder of software giant Microsoft.
-- EU OVERPAID CEREAL PRODUCERS BY 12 BILLION STG

An unpublished report by the British Ministry of Agriculture has calculated the overpayments made by the European Union to cereal farmers over four years to June 1997 at Ecu17 billion. The money was paid as compensation for cuts in price supports under the Common Agricultural Policy.
-- BRITISH BANK LENDING HITS SIX-YEAR HIGH

Figures released by the British Bankers' Association have revealed that bank lending reached the highest quarterly levels for six years in the first three months of 1997. The figures, which reinforce concerns over an unsustainable credit boom, show that lending by banks to the private sector rose to 11.39 billion sterling during the period, up from 6.98 billion stg in the fourth quarter of 1996.
-- BARCLAYS LINK TO CELLNET ENHANCED

Mobile telephone operator Cellnet has said more than 50,000 customers -- some 20 per cent of the company's net new connections -- had taken advantage of an offer made as part of an 18-month alliance with credit card company Barclaycard. Under the offer, Barclaycard customers were offered a special button on Cellnet phones allowing access to financial services as well
as cut price calls.
-- OIL GROUP SOCO SETS SIGHTS ON FULL LISTING IN LONDON

Oil explorer and developer Soco International, which concentrates mainly on Russia and Mongolia, is looking to raise $75 million in a full listing on the London Stock Exchange. Soco has been formed by combining the international interests of U.S.-quoted oil developer Snyder Oil and assets from Cairn Energy. Following the flotation, Soco is expected to have a market capitalisation of about 250 million stg.
-- APV SHARES UP 7.5 PER CENT ON BID APPROACH

Process equipment maker APV has said it had received a bid approach which would lead to an offer for the company. Shares in APV have risen by over 16 per cent in the past week and jumped 7.5 per cent, to 71p, on Tuesday. APV has a current market value of about 211 million sterling and among possible bidders being suggested by analysts for APV are Italy's Sasib and Tomkins of
the UK.
-- U.S. GROUP COULD MOUNT QCH BID

U.S. group Principal Healthcare Investors is reported to be considering a bid for Quality Care Homes. Principal, part of Omega Healthcare Investors, was identified by Duncan Bannatyne, chairman of QCH. Bannatyne also confirmed that he would be willing to sell his 51 per cent stake in the nursing homes group, but cast doubt on whether the negotiations would be
successful.
-- POWDERJECT PLANS TO RAISE 35 MILLION STG IN FLOAT

Powderject Pharmaceuticals, the company formerly known as Oxford Biosciences, is seeking to raise between 30 million stg and 35 million stg in one of Britain's biggest biotech flotations. The float, planned for early June, will value Powderject at more than 100 million stg. The company intends to offer painless injections with a patented device developed by
engineers at Oxford University.
